<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.

Reducing the number of queries for Obihai sensor updates from ~5 per sensor to 1, upgrades pyobihai dependency to 1.4.2 (https://github.com/ejpenney/pyobihai/releases/tag/1.4.2) which introduces query caching for device attributes which never change.

The hope is this will fix https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/91666, but it should at least give better logging about what's happening.

issue_context.title: Obihai integration states "Invalid credentials", but credentials are correct and sensors are updating
issue_context.body:
### The problem

System logs are flooded with "Invalid credentials" errors, however everything about integration appears to be working. I can verify that:
1. I've enabled the local admin password for my Obi200, and gave it a new password
2. I can login locally to the webpage via IP with the "admin" credentials and new password
3. I've added the integration via the UI, using the local IP (I've only ever used the new UI integration; never the YAML config)
4. The integration appears to be working, as all sensors are updating properly and as expected. 

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.4.5

### What was the last working version of Home Assistant Core?

_No response_

### What type of installation are you running?

Home Assistant OS

### Integration causing the issue

obihai

### Link to integration documentation on our website

https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/obihai

### Diagnostics information

[home-assistant_obihai_2023-04-19T11-40-17.870Z.log](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/11272552/home-assistant_obihai_2023-04-19T11-40-17.870Z.log)


### Example YAML snippet

_No response_

### Anything in the logs that might be useful for us?

```txt
Logger: pyobihai
Source: components/obihai/sensor.py:161
First occurred: 7:29:58 AM (48 occurrences)
Last logged: 7:39:46 AM

Invalid credentials
```


### Additional information

_No response_

have you tried restarting the obihai device to see if that corrects the issue?

I've done numerous soft/hard (power off) reboots, and still see the issue. I just did another soft reboot through HA and this is the result:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/15205204/233120965-9d032e79-7a59-432e-b7fd-e1df7c79708c.png)

Yet the device sensors all return to normal and report status correctly.

The invalid_credentials message is given when there's _any_ problem connecting to the Obihai.  And to be clear, it sounds like this issue is intermittent for you?  Looking at your log it seems like it drops out approximately every 8 minutes.  That's one odd coincidence, Obihai is updating several times per minute, so most of the updates work, but then it drops for a minute or so, and resumes working.

I wonder if there's a network instability of some kind between your home assistant and the Obihai?  Are you using a hostname or an IP for the "host" value?  Some OS's (Home Assistant OS included) have some trouble with DNS resolution, and I've found using IPs to be most stable.  I would expect that issue to be less "regular" and more consistent, but it's a place to start.

I initially was using "host" value, but have since deleted it and switched to IP address, and have rebooted both the HA and the Obihai (all before posting the logs). 
And the log I posted earlier was just a quick debug. Since I posted that latest screenshot, there haven't been any errors. I think they show up every time it's reloaded, or I do any upgrades or reboot my HA instance.

It also occurs to me that I've had some issues when testing multiple home assistants talking to one Obihai, the hardware in these things is pretty low-power and gets overwhelmed easily.  Perhaps we should turn down the scan_interval from every 5 seconds, to maybe every 10 or 15?  It's a tricky balance, we want up-to-date data, but we don't want to overwhelm the Obihai with requests.
FWIW, I only have the one Obihai and one HA instance. All connections are local LAN (although I do have the Obihai on its own VLAN, and it's the only device on it).

> I initially was using "host" value, but have since deleted it and switched to IP address, and have rebooted both the HA and the Obihai (all before posting the logs). And the log I posted earlier was just a quick debug. Since I posted that latest screenshot, there haven't been any errors. I think they show up every time it's reloaded, or I do any upgrades or reboot my HA instance.

OK, good info, and glad it's working even if only a little bit better... Currently during reload/restarts we run a few extra authentication queries, I'm trying to get some of this cleaned up in a [future release](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/89121).  I'm going to leave this bug open, we'll check back after those changes get merged/released.  I think it's possible we're just overwhelming your Obihai, and the current query rate is right on the edge of the tolerance.  Hopefully reusing the authentication tokens in future releases will eliminate this error message for you.

Do let us know if the behavior changes in any way though.
OK, I'll try and keep an eye for the updates. Thanks.
